blocks.text: Presented as part of the Festival d’Automne in Paris, Lubaina Himid and Magda Stawarska transform the Chapelle Saint-Louis de la Salpêtrière into a space of collective remembrance and attentive listening.
Their monumental installation, , (Waiting Together), draws on the building’s complex history, examining the tensions between care, confinement, institutional power and female agency.

Sweeping lengths of African Dutch wax fabric, screenprinted with architectural plans and fragments of the human body, extend through the chapel’s nave. One hundred individually named, hand-painted chairs evoke a congregation of women waiting and listening, accompanied by an immersive soundscape of voices counting to sixty in more than thirty languages. Through the interplay of painting, textiles, architecture and sound, the artists consider the significance of waiting as both an individual and collective experience.

Curated by Clément Dirié, the commission continues nearly a decade of collaboration between Himid and Stawarska, bringing together their shared interests in memory, overlooked histories and the relationship between sound and visual experience.
As part of the Festival d’Automne, the Musée d’Art Moderne de Paris also presents Himid’s celebrated life-size cut-out installation A Fashionable Marriage (1986), on view until 10 January 2027.
Attendre ensemble is on at the Chapelle Saint-Louis de la Salpêtrière , Paris, from 6 November until 20 December 2026.
